name: Nasi Kandar Pelita — Jalan Ampang
insider_tip: Order ayam goreng + kuah campur (mixed gravy) — they ladle four curries on top. Skip the rice, get roti canai instead.

name: Saravanaa Bhavan — Brickfields
insider_tip: Banana leaf thali at lunch is unbeatable value. Ask for extra rasam — they'll refill it.

name: Yut Kee Restaurant
insider_tip: Roti babi on Saturday only — get there before 11am or it's gone. Hainanese chicken chop is the all-day winner.

name: Wong Ah Wah — Jalan Alor
insider_tip: Chicken wings are the must-order — char-grilled, not fried. Skip the seafood, prices are tourist-tier.

name: Madras Lane Curry Mee
insider_tip: Stall at the back of Madras Lane — go before 1pm or they sell out. Add the cockles if they have them.

name: Village Park Restaurant — Damansara Uptown
insider_tip: The nasi lemak ayam goreng is legendary — crispy fried chicken with fragrant coconut rice and killer sambal. Go before 11am on weekends or face a 30-min wait

name: Syed Bistro — KL Sentral
insider_tip: The rendang is rich and tender — pair it with sayur lodeh and sambal belacan. Portions are huge so two dishes plus rice is plenty for one person

name: Nasi Lemak Antarabangsa — Kampung Baru
insider_tip: Open from evening till late — the ayam goreng berempah is the star. Grab a spot at the plastic tables under the tent. Cash only, always packed but turnover is fast

name: Rebung Restaurant by Chef Ismail
insider_tip: All-you-can-eat traditional Malay buffet — over 100 dishes daily. The ulam (herb salad) station and gulai kawah (big-pot curry) are what you can't get elsewhere. Go for lunch, it's freshest

name: Gem Restaurant & Lounge — KLCC
insider_tip: Modern Malay fine dining with a view of the Twin Towers. The rendang short rib and buah keluak fried rice are standouts. Book a window table for sunset

name: Al-Rawsha — Jalan Ampang
insider_tip: The mixed grill platter and lamb mandy are massive — share between two. The hummus and fattoush are legit. Open late, great for post-dinner shisha

name: Sahara Tent Restaurant — Ampang
insider_tip: The lamb ouzi (whole roasted lamb on rice) feeds 4-5 people and needs to be pre-ordered. For walk-ins, the chicken shawarma platter and kunafa dessert are the go-to

name: Tarbush Restaurant — Bukit Bintang
insider_tip: One of KL's longest-running Middle Eastern restaurants. The mixed meze platter is the best starter — hummus, baba ganoush, tabbouleh, and warm pita. Lamb kebab is the crowd favourite

name: Kashmir Restaurant — Bukit Bintang
insider_tip: The butter chicken and garlic naan combo is the safe bet. For something special, try the lamb nihari (slow-cooked stew) — rich, spiced, and deeply satisfying. Portions are generous

name: Ambala Restaurant — Ampang
insider_tip: Proper Pakistani home-style cooking — the nihari and paya (trotters stew) are weekend specials. The chapli kebab and biryani are excellent any day. Cheap and filling

name: Karim's by Javed — Bukit Bintang
insider_tip: The mutton biryani is slow-cooked and layered properly — fragrant and rich. The seekh kebab and dal makhani are excellent sides. Weekday lunch is quieter

name: Madam Kwan's — Suria KLCC
insider_tip: The nasi bojari (spiced rice with fried chicken, prawn sambal, and acar) is the signature — every tourist and local orders it. The laksa and satay are solid too

name: Restoran Kin Kin — Chow Kit
insider_tip: Old-school nasi campur spot — point at whatever looks good behind the glass. The curry fish head on Fridays is a local event. Go early, best dishes run out by noon

name: Pak Punjab Restaurant — Chow Kit
insider_tip: The tandoori chicken and daal are outstanding — proper Punjabi flavours. The naan comes fresh off the tandoor. Open late, always busy with the Pakistani community which says it all

name: Khan Jee Restaurant — Chow Kit
insider_tip: Famous for the karahi gosht (wok-fried mutton) and chapli kebab. The biryani sells out fast on weekends so go early. Cheap, filling, and legit Pakistani home cooking

name: Olio — Damansara Jaya, PJ
insider_tip: Great Middle Eastern-Mediterranean fusion. The shakshuka for brunch and the lamb shoulder for dinner are standouts. Portions are proper and the pita bread is baked fresh

name: Darul Makan — Shah Alam
insider_tip: Near the Blue Mosque — perfect pit stop. The nasi kerabu and ayam percik are outstanding. Lunch buffet-style so go early for the widest selection

name: Restoran Halab — Shah Alam
insider_tip: Authentic Syrian food — the chicken shawarma plate and mixed grill are excellent. The fatayer (stuffed pastry) and knafeh dessert are worth ordering every time

name: Mandi & Madfoon House — Shah Alam
insider_tip: The lamb mandi is fall-off-the-bone tender with smoky fragrant rice — order the full portion to share. The haneeth (slow-roasted) is even better if they have it. Busy on weekends, go early
